id.description: Must equal the app's directory name; doubles as the site slug.

description.description: Meta/OG description, one or two sentences.

status.description: The site lists only published apps; the wizard scaffolds drafts too (pre-publish testing).

modules.description: Wizard module ids (what --modules takes), not the site's marketing slugs.

logo.description: App-dir-relative path, e.g. listing/icon.png. Passed to the wizard's brand step. An app-dir-relative path. No dots outside the extension, so it cannot climb out of the app directory - the same shape module.schema.json requires of a module's paths. The wizard also refuses a path that leaves the directory or is a symlink when it reads one (insideProblem); this is the half a catalog's own CI can refuse before anybody fetches it.

env.description: Extra .env lines for the scaffold. Deliberately narrower than module env: no secret, no resolve, no prompt — an app preset must not hook wizard steps or declare secrets.

additionalProperties.description: A semver range or a dist-tag, and nothing else — the same rule module.schema.json states for a module embed, for the same reason. The wizard joins name and version into one npm install argument and runs it, with install scripts, inside the user's own project, so a value carrying ":" or "/" — file:, link:, portal:, workspace:, npm:, git+ssh://, https://, or a bare user/repo — would name a source the manifest is not allowed to choose. parseAppManifest() in the wizard re-checks both patterns: an npx run reaches no schema.

npmDependencies.description: Package names the app preset adds to the scaffold's package.json, mapped to version ranges.

playbook.description: App-dir-relative path to the agent build plan. No dots outside the extension, so it cannot climb out of the app directory.

icon.description: Square PNG, at least 256x256. An app-dir-relative path. No dots outside the extension, so it cannot climb out of the app directory - the same shape module.schema.json requires of a module's paths. The wizard also refuses a path that leaves the directory or is a symlink when it reads one (insideProblem); this is the half a catalog's own CI can refuse before anybody fetches it.

provides.description: What the app itself ships (overlay modules, product surfaces) — rendered on the site beside the wizard modules, so the install section tells the whole truth.
